statement.summary: Proposition 10.2 is frozen as `inversionLaw20Statement` (supplement of 2026-10-22, `S09_CrossoverLaws_Window20.lean`): the group-09 whole statement `inversionLawStatement` — (i) `inversionCompositeStatement`, (ii) `inversionPrimeStatement` (both with the extra antecedent d ≥ 1), `phiSignStatement` (φ as a function of real x via `Real.rpow`: unique zero d_c(p), sign on both sides), `dcAsymptoticStatement` (O(1) as explicit ∃C ∃P₀ over primes) and the window with ∃ C — together with the window with the paper's explicit constant 20 in criteria form (`inversionExplicitWindow20Statement`: the hypotheses of (i)/(ii) hold for d ≤ d_c − 20 resp. d ≥ d_c + 20) and in probability form (`inversionWindow20Statement`). The supplement was frozen after the helper theorems `window_i`/`window_ii` that prove it existed; S09_CrossoverLaws.lean itself is unchanged.
deltas: d ≥ 1 is an explicit antecedent of (i), (ii) and the window Props (Definition 2.1; necessary, see map hyp.d).
φ is `phi p x` on all of ℝ with real powers `Real.rpow`; at d : ℕ it is the paper's expression (`phi_natCast`).
d_c(p) = `dc p` with ln = `Real.log`; log_b = `Real.logb b`; all arguments positive under p ≥ 3, σ ≥ 2.
p^{d−1}, (p+1)^{d−1} use ℕ-subtraction, exact since 1 ≤ d.
O(1) as p → ∞ is rendered as ∃ C ∃ P₀ ∀ prime p ≥ P₀, |d_c(p) − p ln 2| ≤ C (not mathlib's IsBigO; equivalent).

The window is frozen with the paper's explicit 20 in two forms (hypotheses of (i)/(ii) hold; the probability inequalities hold), in the supplement `S09_CrossoverLaws_Window20.lean` (2026-10-22, frozen after the helpers `window_i`/`window_ii` existed). The original group-09 forms with ∃ C remain inside `inversionLawStatement` and are implied (take C = 20).
'the two-dimensional composite advantage' is a name for the phenomenon; no d = 2 claim is formalized.

maps.label: Proposition 10.2 = conjunction of six Props

tex.text:
Let $p\ge3$ be prime, $\sigma\ge2$, and set
$\varphi(d)=(1-\tfrac1p)\,p^d-\tfrac12(p+1)^d$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item if $\varphi(d)>\log_\sigma\bigl(2\log_2(p)\,p^{d-1}\bigr)$, then
$P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{(p+1)^d}>P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{p^d}$ (composite
advantage);
\item if $\varphi(d)<-\log_\sigma\bigl(2\log_2(p{+}1)\,(p{+}1)^{d-1}\bigr)$,
then $P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{(p+1)^d}<P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{p^d}$ (prime
advantage).
\end{enumerate}
The function $\varphi$, regarded as a function of real $d$, is positive
below and negative above its unique zero

so the two-dimensional ``composite advantage'' inverts within an
explicitly bounded window around $d_c(p)$, a dimension that grows
\emph{linearly} in the prime: (i) applies to every integer $d\ge1$ with
$d\le d_c(p)-20$, and (ii) to every integer $d\ge d_c(p)+20$

lean.text:
inversionCompositeStatement ∧ inversionPrimeStatement ∧ phiSignStatement ∧
    dcAsymptoticStatement ∧ inversionExplicitWindowStatement ∧ inversionWindowStatement

maps.note: `inversionLaw20Statement` = the group-09 whole `inversionLawStatement` ((i), (ii), the sign pattern of φ, d_c = p ln 2 + O(1), the window with ∃ C) ∧ the window with the explicit constant 20 in criteria and probability form (supplement of 2026-10-22). The ∃ C conjuncts are implied by the explicit ones. The auxiliary `inversionProofLogRatioStatement` is not part of it.

maps.label: p ≥ 3 prime, σ ≥ 2
maps.note: Antecedents of (i), (ii) and all four window Props. `phiSignStatement` drops σ ≥ 2 (φ and d_c do not involve σ); `dcAsymptoticStatement` quantifies over the primes p ≥ P₀ instead (its p → ∞).

maps.label: d ≥ 1 (implicit in the paper)
maps.note: The paper leaves d ≥ 1 implicit in (i), (ii) and the window (d is a dimension, Definition 2.1); the criteria form of the window states it in the text (map crit.d). The antecedent is necessary: at d = 0 both lattices are a single point, so both probabilities are 0, while the hypothesis of (i) can hold. With the paper's p^{d−1} = p^{−1} this happens already at p = 3, σ = 2 (φ(0) = 1/6 > log₂(2 log₂(3)/3) ≈ 0.079); with Lean's truncated ℕ-subtraction d − 1 = 0 it needs a large alphabet, e.g. p = 3, σ ≥ 1015 or p = 5, σ ≥ 168.

maps.label: φ(d) = (1 − 1/p) p^d − ½ (p+1)^d
maps.note: `phi p x` is defined for real x with `Real.rpow` (positive bases); at x = d : ℕ it equals the paper's expression with natural powers (`phi_natCast`, proved).

maps.label: (i) φ(d) > log_σ(2 log₂(p) p^{d−1}) ⇒ P_{(p+1)^d} > P_{p^d}

lean.text:
Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * Real.logb 2 (p : ℝ) * (p : ℝ) ^ (d - 1)) < phi p (d : ℝ) →
      probUnif p d σ < probUnif (p + 1) d σ

maps.note: Implication with the inequalities written in the < direction.

maps.label: φ(d) > log_σ(2 log₂(p) p^{d−1})

lean.text: Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * Real.logb 2 (p : ℝ) * (p : ℝ) ^ (d - 1)) < phi p (d : ℝ)

maps.note: φ evaluated at the real point (d : ℝ).

maps.label: log_σ(2 log₂(p) p^{d−1})
maps.note: `Real.logb σ`, argument ≥ 2 log₂ 3 > 0; p^{d−1} with ℕ-subtraction, exact as 1 ≤ d.

maps.label: P^unif_{(p+1)^d} > P^unif_{p^d}

lean.text: probUnif p d σ < probUnif (p + 1) d σ

maps.note: Same strict inequality, written with <.

maps.label: P^unif_{m^d}

lean.text: (numSS n d σ : ℝ) / (σ : ℝ) ^ (n ^ d)

maps.note: Shared real-valued definition, used with n = p and n = p + 1.

maps.label: (ii) φ(d) < −log_σ(2 log₂(p+1)(p+1)^{d−1}) ⇒ P_{(p+1)^d} < P_{p^d}

lean.text:
phi p (d : ℝ) <
        -Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * Real.logb 2 ((p : ℝ) + 1) * ((p : ℝ) + 1) ^ (d - 1)) →
      probUnif (p + 1) d σ < probUnif p d σ

maps.note: Same hypotheses p ≥ 3 prime, σ ≥ 2, plus d ≥ 1.

maps.label: φ(d) < −log_σ(2 log₂(p+1)(p+1)^{d−1})

lean.text:
phi p (d : ℝ) <
        -Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * Real.logb 2 ((p : ℝ) + 1) * ((p : ℝ) + 1) ^ (d - 1))

maps.note: φ evaluated at the real point (d : ℝ); the minus sign is real negation.

maps.label: log_σ(2 log₂(p+1)(p+1)^{d−1})
maps.note: p + 1 as the real `(p : ℝ) + 1`; argument ≥ 4 > 0, base σ ≥ 2.

maps.label: P^unif_{(p+1)^d} < P^unif_{p^d}

lean.text: probUnif (p + 1) d σ < probUnif p d σ

maps.note: Same strict inequality.

maps.label: 'composite advantage' / 'prime advantage'

lean.text: probUnif p d σ < probUnif (p + 1) d σ
probUnif (p + 1) d σ < probUnif p d σ

maps.note: Names of the conclusions of (i) and (ii): composite advantage = P_{(p+1)^d} > P_{p^d} (`probUnif p d σ < probUnif (p + 1) d σ`), prime advantage = the reverse. The window sentence uses the first name; the Lean anchors are the two inequalities of the probability-form window Prop, below and above the window.

maps.label: φ (real d) positive below, negative above its unique zero d_c(p)

tex.text:
The function $\varphi$, regarded as a function of real $d$, is positive
below and negative above its unique zero

lean.text:
(∀ x : ℝ, phi p x = 0 ↔ x = dc p) ∧
      (∀ x : ℝ, x < dc p → 0 < phi p x) ∧
      (∀ x : ℝ, dc p < x → phi p x < 0)

maps.note: For every real x: φ(x) = 0 ↔ x = d_c(p) (the unique zero, and it is d_c), φ > 0 left of it, φ < 0 right of it. Hypotheses p prime, p ≥ 3; σ dropped (not involved).

maps.label: unique zero

lean.text: ∀ x : ℝ, phi p x = 0 ↔ x = dc p

maps.note: Existence and uniqueness in one iff, with the zero identified as `dc p`.

maps.label: d_c(p) = ln(2 − 2/p)/ln(1 + 1/p)
maps.note: ln = `Real.log`; for p ≥ 3 both arguments are positive and the denominator is > 0.

maps.label: d_c(p) = p ln 2 + O(1) (p → ∞)

lean.text: ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ P₀ : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → P₀ ≤ p → |dc p - p * Real.log 2| ≤ C

maps.note: O(1) as p → ∞ through the primes, in explicit ∃C ∃P₀ form (not `Asymptotics.IsBigO`). Equivalent to the paper's claim. The proof in fact gives C = 2, P₀ = 2, i.e. a bound for every prime.

maps.label: the 2D composite advantage inverts within a bounded window around d_c(p)

tex.text:
so the two-dimensional ``composite advantage'' inverts within an
explicitly bounded window around $d_c(p)$

lean.text:
((d : ℝ) ≤ dc p - 20 → probUnif p d σ < probUnif (p + 1) d σ) ∧
      (dc p + 20 ≤ (d : ℝ) → probUnif (p + 1) d σ < probUnif p d σ)

maps.note: Probability form with the explicit 20: composite advantage for d ≤ d_c − 20, prime advantage for d ≥ d_c + 20, so the inversion happens inside (d_c − 20, d_c + 20) ('inverts within an explicitly bounded window'). Uniform in p ≥ 3 and σ ≥ 2.

maps.label: 'the two-dimensional' composite advantage
maps.note: Names the phenomenon (Observation 10.5 / the 2019 paper); no claim about d = 2 is frozen here (at p = 3 there is no 2D composite advantage, consistent with the statement).

maps.label: a dimension that grows linearly in the prime

tex.text:
a dimension that grows
\emph{linearly} in the prime

maps.note: Refers to the location d_c(p), not the window width; covered by `dcAsymptoticStatement`.

maps.label: (i) applies for d ≤ d_c(p) − 20, (ii) for d ≥ d_c(p) + 20

tex.text:
(i) applies to every integer $d\ge1$ with
$d\le d_c(p)-20$, and (ii) to every integer $d\ge d_c(p)+20$

lean.text:
((d : ℝ) ≤ dc p - 20 →
        Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * Real.logb 2 (p : ℝ) * (p : ℝ) ^ (d - 1)) < phi p (d : ℝ)) ∧
      (dc p + 20 ≤ (d : ℝ) →
        phi p (d : ℝ) <
          -Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * Real.logb 2 ((p : ℝ) + 1) * ((p : ℝ) + 1) ^ (d - 1)))

maps.note: '(i) applies' = the hypothesis of (i) holds (criteria form); (i) then gives the composite advantage, and (ii) the prime advantage.

maps.label: the constant 20
maps.note: Frozen literally since the supplement of 2026-10-22: `dc p - 20` and `dc p + 20` in both window forms. Provenance: the 20 was added to the paper in v4 (PAPER_CORRECTIONS_PROPOSAL.md, entry 22) from the helper theorems `window_i`/`window_ii`, and frozen afterwards, so unlike the Phase H statements it was not frozen before its proof existed. The original group-09 window Props say only ∃ C (map wexists).

maps.note: Group 09 was frozen against the v3.1 text ('an explicitly bounded window'), so its two window Props say ∃ C. They are kept unchanged inside `inversionLawStatement` and follow from the C = 20 forms (take C = 20). Not a separate paper claim.
